posts.summary: Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority says AI-controlled traffic signals should reduce congestion by at least 10%.

posts.summary: Sheikh Hamdan launched what Dubai calls the world's first city-wide tourism loyalty programme. An invitation-only tourism club and streamlined visa services also begin in November.

posts.summary: Work has begun on two new bridges on Palm Jumeirah to improve access to the island.

posts.summary: The Technology Innovation Institute is partnering with France's Naval Group on autonomous underwater systems.

posts.why_it_matters: US rules often shape global vendor terms; expect more compliance requirements in AI tools Aldar buys.

posts.summary: Google plans to turn off Search access for schools that opt out of its AI. The plan drew wide criticism, covered by 63 outlets, alongside a lawsuit over AI harm to a student.
posts.why_it_matters: Aldar Education needs clear AI policies and vendor-independence plans as big tech links core tools to AI adoption.

viral.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
viral.views_source: No dated source gave a figure.
viral.what_shows: OpenAI's automated system flagged 2,308 possible Linux kernel flaws, reproduced 1,724, and built working root-access attacks for 948. The run cost about $1.21M, roughly $1,279 per working attack, versus 166 flaws in July.
viral.what_behind: Figures are OpenAI's own, read via The Neuron. Partial outside backing: Linux maintainers patched 61 flaws, 43 more fixes in preparation. Attacks need existing machine access; fixes need expert review. Related GPT-5.6 Cyber model limited to US government.
viral.aldar_fit_area: IT and building-systems security across malls, offices and logistics sites (embedded Linux in BMS, access control, CCTV, IoT)
viral.leadership_line: AI is making it far cheaper to find software holes, so we're checking that our building-systems vendors can patch quickly.
viral.assessed_from: OpenAI's own published figures via The Neuron summary, plus partial outside validation through accepted Linux patches.
